_README: Dates on which a real bug was FOUND in each bot's live path, newest last.
This replaced a git-log heuristic (--grep='^Fix') that was materially
wrong: most of this project's genuine fixes do not say 'Fix' in the
subject ('research_agent: drop price-action keywords', 'Record the
actual fill on entry'), and --grep searches the message BODY too, so it
also matched commits that were not fixes at all. It reported Main as 12
days stable and Sofi as 25 when both were 2 -- it flattered the bots,
which is the worst direction for a readiness signal to be wrong in.
There is no reliable lexical pattern for 'this commit fixed a bug', so
this is explicit rather than inferred. The cost is that it depends on
being updated; that is the same discipline LESSONS.md already relies on,
and a missing entry now fails loudly (stale date) rather than silently
reading as stability.
Record the date the bug was FOUND, not when the fix shipped -- the
question is how long the code has gone without a defect surfacing.
2026-09-23: 'prod' and 'trading2' now run THE SAME CODE. alpaca-bot
was retired and Main's account is traded by /opt/nova-main, a clone of
/opt/trading-2-0 at the same commit. So a bug found in Nova's code is a
bug in Main's code too, and must be logged under BOTH keys -- they are
two deployments, not two codebases. Only 'sofi' still has a codebase of
its own. The pre-2026-09-23 'prod' entries below belong to the retired
dual-signal scanner and are kept as history, not as a claim about the
code running there now.

prod.what: research_agent vetoed on articles that never named the tagged company
research_agent price-action keywords ('plunge') blocked entries on bullish articles
research_agent 'crash' vetoed index ETFs on bullish market-crash headlines; _INDEX_ETF_TICKERS needs 2+ tags and this was tagged to SPY alone
market_hours_notifier saved its state file BEFORE sending the Telegram ping, so one transient send failure lost an open/close notification permanently (notification path, not the trading path)

Stops are enforced by the 60s poll loop, not resting at the broker, so 89% of losing trades exit BEYOND their stop -- mean 1.61x planned risk (median 1.14x, worst 7.94x). The bot's stated 0.5% risk per trade is therefore wrong by ~61%, and break-even win rate rises from 35.7% to 47.2% against an observed 41.7%. Found at size on nova-main day one.

await_fill returned on the FIRST PARTIAL rather than waiting for a terminal status, so a large order filling in stages had its first slice journalled as the whole trade. 7 of 9 rows on the $100k account were wrong -- MSFT 20.0 against an actual 49.92, TSLA 42.0 against 65.73 -- and one trade was recorded as a $19 LOSS when it was a $265 WIN. Closed P&L read +$29.97 against a real +$213.30. Invisible at $50 (a $12 order fills in one tick); only orders worth thousands fill in stages.
